plan_a_advantages: More emphasis on building a strong endurance base through longer runs.
Includes more targeted hill work, directly relevant to trail running.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates cross-training for aerobic stimulus with reduced impact.
Includes a dedicated strength and mobility session, which can be beneficial for injury prevention and overall performance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes building a strong base of endurance through longer, easier runs, alongside targeted hill work, which is crucial for trail running. Plan B, while including tempo and hill sessions, focuses more heavily on threshold training and strength work, which could lead to burnout or over-reliance on specific efforts without sufficient foundational endurance. Plan A’s consistent emphasis on longer, lower-intensity runs will better prepare the athlete for the sustained effort required in trail races, while Plan B’s more intense sessions could be detrimental if the athlete isn't already at a high enough fitness level.
